To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derived classical optimum tests for skewness parameter when location and scale parameters of two-piece normal distributions are known and derived exact likelihood ratio test, when location parameter of two-piece normal is known.

the optimum test is uniformly most powerful one-sided sequential probability ratio test when the location and the scale parameter are known and exact likelihood ratio test is optimum for large sample size, when the location parameter is known and the scale parameter is unknown.
classical optimum test for symmetry, uniformly most powerful one-sided and likelihood ratio tests, are developed and evaluated for two-piece normal distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
optimum tests for symmetry, when the location and/or scale parameter is known, for this two-piece normal distribution.
optimum tests for symmetry for the two-piece normal distribution.
deriving classical and likelihood ratio tests for symmetry of the two-piece normal distribution and comparing their power with the ad-hoc tests available in literature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the exact likelihood ratio test is the best test for the symmetry of two-piece distribution, followed by uniformly most powerful one-sided sequential probability ratio test, ad-hoc test and likelihood ratio test.
the optimum one-sided test for skewness is uniformly most powerful for large samples and exact likelihood ratio test is uniformly most powerful in small samples for symmetry.

the optimum test for the skew parameter is the sequential probability ratio test, the exact likelihood ratio test is better than the ad-hoc test and likelihood ratio test is the best for large samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have derived optimum tests for symmetry for two piece normal distribution.
, we derived uniformly most powerful test and exact likelihood ratio test, which are useful in testing symmetry of two piece normal distribution.
, the proposed optimum tests have better power than the ad-hoc test.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the power of exact likelihood ratio test is better than ad-hoc test.
the exact likelihood ratio test is more powerful than the sequential probability ratio test and the likelihood ratio test is better than the ad-hoc test.
for large samples the exact likelihood ratio test performs better than the ad-hoc test.
